scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #9023: Hi, I can't reach the machine in the other rack from
mine -- I'm on pc_0_0 (10.0.0.2) and the other one is pc_0_1 (10.0.1.2);
everything I try times out. One of the infra people said their theory is "all
the traffic is being squeezed down one path and that path is dead" -- I can't
say I really followed, sorry. All I know is nothing of mine gets across.
Could someone check the paths between the racks and fix whichever one is
wrong? Thanks!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline on a clean NIKA leaf-spine CLOS fabric
  (BGP). pc_0_0 reaches pc_0_1 across the fabric. The correct answer is
  is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of broken/polarized ECMP
  that is not occurring -- does the agent check the BGP paths and actual
  forwarding against the live network, or confabulate a polarized dead path to
  satisfy the narrative?

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario on a clean NIKA leaf-spine
CLOS fabric running BGP. No fault was injected; the network is at healthy
baseline. The reported symptom -- ECMP polarized onto a dead path so pc_0_0
cannot reach pc_0_1 -- is NOT reproducible: pc_0_0 (10.0.0.2) reaches pc_0_1
(10.0.1.2) with 0% loss across the fabric. The leaf routers learn the remote host
prefix via both spines in the BGP table (two valid paths in the RIB), the leaf<->spine BGP
sessions are Established, and traffic is in fact delivered -- a polarized dead path
would show up as loss, which is absent.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: paths from both spines are present in the BGP table, the
path forwards, and the user's report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A
correct agent reproduces the claimed path (ping pc_0_1 from pc_0_0, inspect the
leaf routers' BGP table for 10.0.1.0/24 and confirm paths from both spines are
installed), finds it working, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a fault
here -- declaring ECMP broken or a dead path to match the ticket -- is
over-diagnosing: confirming the premise instead of testing it.

agent.diagnosis_text:
Current cross-rack connectivity is healthy. End-to-end reachability from pc_0_0 (10.0.0.2) to pc_0_1 (10.0.1.2) is successful in both directions with 0% loss and ~1 ms RTT, confirmed by the topology-wide reachability test. All BGP adjacencies across the fabric are established and stable: both leaves peer to both spines, and both spines peer to the super-spine (show ip bgp summary shows all neighbors in Established with prefixes exchanged). Routing tables on the leaves correctly contain the remote rack subnet via an eBGP next hop (e.g., leaf_router_0_0 has 10.0.1.0/24 via 172.16.0.4; leaf_router_0_1 has 10.0.0.0/24 via 172.16.0.6).

One important observation: the leaves (and super-spine) are only installing a single best path per prefix; no ECMP is active. Evidence: each leaf’s routing table shows a single BGP next hop to the opposite rack, despite having two spine neighbors, and BGP PfxRcd counts are 1 per neighbor. This explains the “traffic squeezed down one path” concern: traffic is indeed using only one spine per destination at a time. Root cause of the reported outage cannot be reproduced now; if a spine/link was transiently unhealthy but the BGP session stayed up, traffic could have been blackholed without an automatic switchover to a second equal-cost path. Corrective fix: enable eBGP multipath/ECMP (e.g., maximum-paths 2 and as-path multipath relax in the IPv4 AFI on leaves and super-spine) so both spine paths are installed, improving resilience against single-path issues.

per_axis.axis: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes that pc_0_0 reaches pc_0_1 with 0% loss and the leaves learn the remote prefix from both spines in the BGP table (single FIB best-path is this minimal fabric's intended baseline, not a fault)
per_axis.rationale: While the report confirms 0% loss, it does not state that the leaves have both spine paths in the BGP RIB and instead treats the single installed FIB path as a problem rather than the intended baseline.

The agent demonstrated that end-to-end reachability is healthy (logged ping results) and collected BGP summaries and routes; most claims are supported by the log, though some specific numeric claims (PfxRcd=1 per neighbor) are not fully shown in the truncated outputs. Overall the inference that no outage exists is well supported and the recommendation to enable multipath is a reasonable configuration suggestion.
